title: Conversation Conduit translation layer for Chat Completions interoperability
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We need a lightweight translation layer that enables Redwood's v2 chat API to accept and respond to OpenAI Chat Completions (v1) request/response shapes with minimal behavioural delta. Goal is to provide a conservative, observable adapter that preserves streaming semantics, tool/function-calling fidelity, and structured output hints while avoiding heavy-weight emulation.

Scope:
- Input mapping: map OpenAI CC request fields (messages, temperature, max_tokens, function specs) to Redwood runtime route and model selection.
- Streaming map: translate chunked SSE/progressive token stream into Redwood streaming frames while preserving function call token boundaries and chunk ids for client reconstructions.
- Function/tool calling: support OpenAI-style functions schema by mapping to Redwood tool hooks, emit explicit tool-invoke events and final function_return channels.
- Structured outputs: honor content-type/structured_output hints, synthesize schema validation errors back into the OpenAI shape.
- Telemetry: add span tags for migrated requests, include mapping diff in debug logs.

Acceptance criteria:
1) A Redwood-hosted endpoint accepts a canonical OpenAI ChatCompletions JSON request and returns parity responses for our E2E test prompts (see tests/conduit/parity-suite).
2) For streaming requests, client-facing chunk_ids and fncall boundaries are stable and deterministic across retries.
3) Tool/function calls triggered by model are emitted through existing toolhook interface with preserved name/args and replayable call ids.
4) Observe <5% p99 latency delta vs native API for small requests (<=128 tokens) in synthetic benchmark.
5) Feature gated behind runtime flag and behind API compatibility header; gradual rollout plan included.

Technical approach:
- Implement an adapter service (stateless per request) that performs lightweight canonicalization: normalizes message role aliases, collapses system/assistant role variants, and maps function specs into Redwood tool metadata.
- For streaming: use a 2-layer envelope: the outer layer is Redwood stream frames, inner payload preserves OpenAI chunk meta (partial, delta, finish_reason, fn_call_token). This avoids re-tokenization on the client.
- For fncalls: when model emits a function call event, the adapter will create a tool invocation record with a deterministic call_id and forward to tool router. Tool results re-injected as assistant messages with the original fn call signature and a synthetic finish_reason.
- Structured output: validate model JSON against sent schema using the same lightweight validator used by the Optimize eval harness; on validation error, synthesize an assistant message with 'structured_output_error' annotation that maps to OpenAI's error conventions.

Design trade-offs and decisions:
- Decision: prefer minimal transform strategy (no language-model re-generation) to reduce latency and preserve semantics.
- Trade-off: some advanced OpenAI client behaviors (e.g., non-deterministic role aliasing) will not be emulated; we document these differences in the compatibility doc.
- Rollout: start as experimental flag 'compat.conduit.v1' for internal customers, then soft-launch to a small set of external customers.

Compatibility and backward-compat checks:
- Create a parity test harness with real-world prompts that exercise function calls, nested JSON outputs, and streaming cancelation.
- Add golden traces for both streaming and non-streaming sequences and run nightly diff job.

Telemetry and observability:
- Add span attributes: conduit.mapping_version, conduit.request_shape_hash, conduit.fncall_count.
- Emit mapping-diff diagnostic artifact to S3 for failing parity tests.

Security & privacy:
- No request body mutation beyond metadata mapping; function payloads forwarded encrypted in transit.
- Confirmed KMS compatibility for tool arguments that reference customer secrets.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement adapter behind feature flag; internal QA run (week 1).
2) Canary to 5% of traffic for compatibility header 'x-rw-compat: openai-cc-v1' (week 2).
3) Expand to select customers (week 3) and monitor cost/latency/quality metrics.
4) Document known incompatibilities and opt-in deprecation path.

Delivery artifacts:
- Design doc: https://docs.internal.redwood/conversation-conduit/spec-v1 (design doc draft)
- Parity test suite: https://qa.internal.redwood/parity/conduit-suite
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/12345, https://github.com/redwood/console/pull/9876

Notes for reviewers: pay attention to streaming frame envelope shape and fncall replay id determinism.
